# Cycle for Change

> cycleforchange.org is a group-ride finder: 1,423 weekly group rides in 19 countries, every one checked at its source and stamped with the date it was last checked; a 2027 calendar of 640 US rides and races; 16 town guides for riders traveling with a bike; a free ride briefing tool; and the story behind it — Robert Castan rides 10,000 miles in 2027, all on the bike.

How a ride gets listed and stays listed: the host's own page, feed or event listing is read and what it says is recorded — day, start time, start point, pace, whether the group waits — with the evidence and the date. A ride checked in the last 90 days is fresh. At 90 days the row says "confirm with the host"; at 150 it leaves the lists and its page says so. Nothing is listed from memory, and a ride nobody has checked is never stamped as checked. Rider reports and a weekly watcher flag rides whose pages changed or vanished. Every ride page says how it was checked, from what, and when.

Money for the organizations Robert rides for goes through their own rides and donation pages, never through this site. Nothing on the site needs an account, and the ride briefing keeps your file in your browser.

## Find a ride

- [Group rides](https://cycleforchange.org/rides/): 1,423 weekly rides, by state, city, day and who they're for (no-drop, beginner, LGBTQ+, women/trans/femme, BIPOC, family, gravel, e-bike). 193 city hubs.
- [Find a ride by kind](https://cycleforchange.org/find-a-ride/): the front door — group rides, events, gravel, a ride briefing.
- [Tonight](https://cycleforchange.org/tonight/): what's rolling near you in the next twelve hours, soonest first.
- [How the list works](https://cycleforchange.org/rides/about/): the checking rules, the freshness clock, what the marks mean.
- [Add a ride](https://cycleforchange.org/rides/add/): the form hosts and riders use.

## Events and the 2027 calendar

- [2027 calendar](https://cycleforchange.org/events/2027/): 640 US rides and races, by month and kind. A date is marked confirmed only when the organizer published it; otherwise it says projected and names the year it is projected from.
- [Events](https://cycleforchange.org/events/): the deep event pages — route, weather, lodging, registration.
- [The rides Robert is doing](https://cycleforchange.org/events/2027/riding/): Center Ride Out (Los Angeles LGBT Center, April 2027) and Cycle to Zero (San Francisco AIDS Foundation, May 2027).

## Towns

- [Town guides](https://cycleforchange.org/towns/): 16 towns for a rider arriving with a bike — shops, the rides, routes, coffee, where to sleep with the bike, how to get the bike there.

## Tools

- [Ride briefing](https://cycleforchange.org/brief/): drop a GPX, TCX or FIT file; get the climbs, the weather at each point at the hour you reach it, what to wear, how much water, and when you're back. Free, no account, nothing stored. Compare two routes on one chart.

## Guides and writing

- [Guides](https://cycleforchange.org/guides/): 22 guides — tires, wheels and hubs, and charity rides (picking one, getting ready, raising the money).
- [Field notes](https://cycleforchange.org/field-notes/): routes and rides from the road, in Robert's words.
- [Journal](https://cycleforchange.org/journal/): his raw writing.
- [Resources](https://cycleforchange.org/resources/): queer mental-health resources. 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; the Trevor Project 1-866-488-7386.

## The story

- [Home](https://cycleforchange.org/): Robert Castan rides 10,000 miles in 2027, all on the bike. The miles counted on the site are miles since June 1, 2026; the count restarts January 1, 2027. Cycling changed his life; he'd like to say he cycles for everyone else, and he's really cycling for himself. The organizations he rides for: one·n·ten (Phoenix), the Los Angeles LGBT Center, the San Francisco AIDS Foundation.
- [What do you cycle for?](https://cycleforchange.org/cyclefor/): five seconds on video from riders he meets.
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/cycl_eforchange/

## Trust

- [How rides are checked](https://cycleforchange.org/methodology/): the source-plus-date rule, the 90-and-150-day clock, the Monday watcher, what software does and what people do.
- [Privacy](https://cycleforchange.org/privacy/): what the site keeps (analytics, five forms), where it goes, and how to take something back. No accounts, no email list, no ads.
- [Contact](https://cycleforchange.org/contact/): Instagram DM; the domain takes no mail.

## Machine-readable

- [Sitemap index](https://cycleforchange.org/sitemap.xml)
- [Feed](https://cycleforchange.org/feed.xml): guides, field notes, event and town pages, newest first.
- Every ride page has an .ics file and Event JSON-LD when the next date is known; every event and town page has JSON-LD that matches the page.
